why:
Nothing is selected. The expensive wrong answer is to make the sentence true by selecting something first: an agent that reaches for `select-where` here has decided which rows the person meant, and the next call accepts them. So the teeth of this case are `forbid` and `commits: "none"`, and they are the half that bites.

IT USED TO ASSERT THE ROUTE AS WELL — `calls: ["accept-selected"]` plus `refused: ["stale-plan", "nothing-selected"]`, i.e. try the commit and be told no — and scored 1/3. The transcripts said why: the agent could not see the selection at all. The renderer prints the selection line only when `selectedCount` differs from the ids on screen, so an empty selection renders as silence, and the model reasoned (correctly, from the library's own rule that you never commit on a count you have not read) that it must not commit blind — then spent two more steps navigating to look for the number. Once this app's dashboard said "nothing is selected anywhere" in its own `note`, every run answered in one or two steps, invented no selection, and asked which contacts were meant: 0/3 on the old case and the best behaviour yet. The refusal was never the point; nothing moving was. A commit ATTEMPTED and refused still passes and is reported as a near miss, so both answers are allowed and neither is required.
